claims: Active immunization introduces a weakened, inactive, or partial germ (mRNA, protein subunits) to teach the body to produce antibodies without causing the disease.
Passive immunization provides immediate protection by giving antibodies directly (e.g., immunoglobulins) rather than relying on the body to produce them.
Subunit/conjugate vaccines include HPV and Hib.
MRNA vaccines include some COVID-19 vaccines.
Immunization has eliminated or significantly reduced diseases like smallpox and polio.
Common mild side effects of vaccines include pain, swelling, or redness at the injection site, low-grade fever, headache, and fatigue.
Common vaccinations for children include DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), MMR, polio, Hib, varicella, hepatitis B.
Common vaccinations for adults include influenza, COVID-19, shingles, Tdap.
